# HEIC test evidence

`checker-1024.heic` is a synthetic 1024x1024 achromatic checkerboard, encoded by
Apple macOS `sips` as a 2x2 grid of HEVC tiles. Its pixels are generated by the
upstream Python script, not taken from a photograph. Source: Thomas Braun's
[heic-rs fixture corpus](https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs/tree/999470f514c8e9a1a7c37ea44ba70cc32b1308fe/tests/fixtures),
commit `999470f514c8e9a1a7c37ea44ba70cc32b1308fe`.

Upstream licenses this generated fixture MIT OR Apache-2.0. This copy uses the
MIT option; the required notice is in [LICENSE-MIT](LICENSE-MIT).

SHA-256: `f24a3b6ae495605e179bd34ae282047dcc4581819eb53041db34c9fdb66648cd`.
The tests also mutate its zero-valued `irot` property to exercise a real
counter-clockwise rotation. They compare decoded pixels against exactly one
rotation and verify JPEG derivative creation.

Run reproducible, offline tests from the repository root:

```powershell
cargo test --locked -p open-tappd-api --lib routes::tasting_photos::
```

## External real iPhone check

An unmodified iPhone 12 Pro portrait photograph was tested on 2026-10-28:
[Greyhounds looking for a table](https://heic.digital/samples/), by Marc from
[Brottdog](https://www.brottdog.com/). The publisher explicitly permits testing,
development and educational use, including commercial software testing, without
attribution. It is not redistributed here; the download retains the camera's
original metadata. This testing permission is separate from the MIT synthetic
fixture license above.

Download: <https://heic.digital/download-sample/greyhounds-looking-for-a-table.heic>

Size: 1,721,433 bytes. SHA-256:
`65960bf2782cd8ebd29a958e75b6adb7dff2bbff841389e869d917438c729010`.
The file has 48 tiles, 4032x3024 coded dimensions and HEIF `irot` counter-clockwise
90 degrees. The guarded backend produces 3024x4032 pixels, a 320x426 thumbnail
and a 960x1280 large JPEG. The unguarded decoder was also compared against an
Apple reference PNG on upstream's `photo-2048.heic`: RGB PSNR 48.22 dB.

To repeat the optional real-device check, download it to a local directory,
verify the checksum above and explicitly select it:

```powershell
$env:HEIC_IPHONE_FIXTURE = 'C:\path\greyhounds-looking-for-a-table.heic'
cargo test --locked -p open-tappd-api --lib --features external-heic-fixture-tests real_iphone_12_pro_portrait
Remove-Item Env:HEIC_IPHONE_FIXTURE
```

## Accepted subset and limits

The decoder is exactly pinned to `heic-rs =0.1.4`, with its thread-pool feature
disabled. It adds no native libraries or new compiler requirements. The existing
two-worker limit covers HEIC too. The API sniffs the container rather than
trusting a filename or MIME type.

Before pixel decoding, every referenced grid tile's uncropped SPS dimensions
are checked. Repeated tile references count toward the aggregate pixel budget.
The backend accepts the reviewed 4:2:0, 8-to-10-bit still-image subset with one
VPS/SPS/PPS per coded tile, at most 256 tiles, no auxiliary alpha image and at
most three primary transforms. Unsupported features fail closed with a JPEG
export suggestion. This does not claim support for all HEIF codecs or sequences.

The 40MP ceiling applies to the primary coded size, transformed output, each
internal SPS and aggregate tile sizes. A separate conservative 192MiB buffer
budget includes retained tile frames, one tile's workspace, orientation copies,
compressed data and bookkeeping. Some HEIC images above 12MP can therefore be
refused even when a JPEG of the same dimensions would fit. Derivative sizing,
JPEG qualities, original-data removal and owner-only access are unchanged.
